content_units: You have a realistic path into a   data-focused, low-code role within 9 months  . Given your background in   retail operations  , your best-fit targets are roles that value reporting, process improvement, stakeholder communication, and KPI ownership more than software engineering.
Best overall fit for your constraints:
-   Operations/Data Analyst   — strongest match to your retail experience
-   BI/Reporting Analyst   — best salary upside with manageable technical depth
-   Commercial or Pricing Analyst   — strong fit if you can show Excel-based business thinking
-   Customer Insights/CRM Analyst   — good option if you like behavior, segmentation, and storytelling
Role Type   Typical Dublin Salary   Coding Load   Why It Fits Your Background   Main Skill Gaps   Fastest Path In

Operations Analyst / Data Analyst     EUR 38k-48k     Low   Retail ops experience maps directly to KPIs, staffing, inventory, service metrics   SQL basics; dashboarding; metrics storytelling   Build 2-3 retail ops projects in Excel/Power BI; target retail, logistics, hospitality, support ops teams

BI Analyst / Reporting Analyst     EUR 40k-52k     Low-Medium   Focus on reports, dashboards, recurring business reporting rather than heavy coding   Power BI; stronger SQL; data modeling basics   Learn Power BI + SQL joins; create executive dashboard portfolio; apply to analyst/reporting roles in larger firms

Commercial Analyst / Pricing Analyst     EUR 38k-50k     Low   Uses Excel, forecasting, margin analysis, promotions, sales performance   Financial/commercial analysis language; forecasting; visualization   Build pricing and sales analysis case studies from retail scenarios; target FMCG, ecommerce, telecom, travel

CRM Analyst / Customer Insights Analyst     EUR 38k-48k     Low-Medium   Sociology + retail gives you a strong angle on customer behavior and segmentation   SQL for customer data; campaign metrics; A/B testing concepts   Learn retention/funnel metrics; build customer segmentation and churn projects; target ecommerce and consumer brands
Best match for your background and timeline.
- Your retail operations experience is already evidence of process ownership, KPI tracking, scheduling, stock/service trade-offs, and cross-team coordination.
- Employers often accept lighter technical depth here if business understanding is strong.
- Fastest route to   EUR 38k+   with the least reinvention.
- Very marketable in Dublin if you can demonstrate   Power BI + SQL + business reporting  .
- Slightly more technical than operations analysis, but still far from heavy coding.
Good if you enjoy numbers, margin thinking, and decision support.
- Retail background gives you credibility in promotions, basket behavior, staffing/productivity, and store performance.
- Excel matters a lot here; advanced business logic can outweigh coding.
Option 4: CRM Analyst / Customer Insights Analyst
Good niche if you want customer behavior rather than operational reporting.
- Your sociology degree is genuinely relevant for segmentation, behavior patterns, and insight storytelling.
- Usually requires some comfort with SQL and marketing/customer metrics.
- Turning messy business problems into KPI dashboards
- Month 1-2: Excel upgrade: pivots, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, charts, basic forecasting
- Month 2-4: SQL essentials: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, JOIN
- Month 3-5: Build one portfolio project on store performance, one on staffing/productivity, one on inventory or sales trends
- Month 5-9: Apply to retail, logistics, customer support, and operations analyst jobs
- Learn Power BI end-to-end: data import, relationships, DAX basics, dashboard layout
- Build 2 polished dashboards: executive sales dashboard and weekly operations report
- Practice explaining insights in business language, not technical jargon
- Target reporting roles in larger companies where process and stakeholder skills matter
- Margin, revenue, promotion, and forecast terminology
- Some employers prefer stronger Excel than SQL
- Learn contribution margin, pricing impact, promo uplift, basket size, and sales variance analysis
- Build a pricing/promotion case study from a retail dataset
- Tailor CV toward decision support, cost control, and performance improvement
- Apply to consumer, ecommerce, telecom, airline, and FMCG analyst roles
- Learn CRM metrics: CAC, retention, repeat purchase, churn, open/click/conversion rates
- Build one customer segmentation project and one churn-risk dashboard
- Position your sociology degree as strength in behavior analysis and pattern interpretation
- Focus on ecommerce, subscription, digital marketing, and consumer businesses
- Learn beginner SQL well enough for reporting:
- Create   3 business-focused projects  , ideally from retail-style scenarios:
- Put them on GitHub or a simple Notion/site with screenshots and short business summaries
- Apply to   entry analyst, reporting, operations, BI junior, commercial analyst, and insights analyst   roles
- Prepare stories using your current experience:
- Be ready to explain one dashboard and one SQL query in plain English
- Operations and reporting roles best leverage your existing retail credibility.
- They are the most defensible “career changer” story.
- They usually do not require Python or advanced engineering skills at entry level.
- They give you a platform to move into better-paid BI or insights roles later.
-   EUR 38k   is achievable for entry/junior analyst roles if you present solid business evidence and a credible portfolio.
- Titles vary a lot; many suitable jobs may not include “data analyst” in the title.
